paper.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix B
paper.note: Strategy paper for 2026/27 to 2028/29. Two companion papers from the same 9 February 2026 G&A meeting also read: doc 226479 (5pp covering report for the strategy) and doc 226476 (4pp Q3 2025/26 covering report). The Q3 detailed appendix (Appendix A of doc 226476) is not bundled in the covering PDF and is not on disk — anything on loan-level movements, weighted rate on the book, or maturity buckets by percentage would sit there. Onward to Council 26 February 2026.

facts.value: Total borrowing £212,022,508 at 8 January 2026 — PWLB £167,522,508, other local authorities £34,500,000, market (banking-sector) £10,000,000, all fixed-rate. Investments: £42,000,000, all short-term. 25% market-loan cap policy, currently at 4.72%.
facts.note: The paper prints no weighted rate on the PWLB book, no maturity profile by band, no loan-by-loan schedule. The three lines sum to £212,022,508 exactly. Ties to £212.0m external borrowing at 31 December 2025 quoted in the Q3 covering report doc 226476 §3.5.

facts.value: Loans CFR grows from £234.188m at 31.3.25 (actual) to £253.167m (31.3.26 est), £282.603m (31.3.27), £290.249m (31.3.28) and £291.933m (31.3.29) — a £57.745m increase across the strategy period. Gross CFR peaks at £335.748m in 31.3.28. OLTL declines £54.302m → £41.892m as PFI/leases run off.
facts.note: Table 6 foots exactly: Gross CFR less OLTL = Loans CFR each year. Movement in loans CFR = financing need less MRP/VRP each year, foots exactly.

facts.value: Over-borrowed by £2.898m at 31.3.25 actual — becomes under-borrowed by £23.181m at 31.3.26 estimate. A £26.079m swing to an internally-borrowed position inside a single year, then broadly held at that level: −£22.723m (26/27), −£21.727m (27/28), −£20.811m (28/29).
facts.note: Table 7 arithmetic ties exactly. External borrowing dropped £19.5m April to December 2025 (doc 226476 §3.5 verbatim). That accounts for most of the swing. The strategy at page 4 states the choice explicitly: 'it is therefore likely to be more cost effective over the medium-term to either use internal resources, or to borrow short-term and medium-term loans instead'.

facts.value: Rises from £206.161m at 31.3.25 to £225.167m (31.3.26 est), £254.603m (31.3.27), £262.249m (31.3.28) and £263.933m (31.3.29). Balance-sheet resources held constant at £38.000m; liquidity allowance £10.000m throughout.
facts.note: Loans CFR row in Table 4 matches Table 6 exactly. Arlingclose chart on page 7 shows the existing fixed-rate loan book running off from c.£200m in 2024 to c.£80m by 2032 and then continuing to decline — the gap between that and the liability-benchmark line is the future new-borrowing requirement.

facts.value: Financing costs to net revenue stream: 5.81% (24/25 actual), 5.66% (25/26 forecast), 6.10% (26/27 budget), 6.38% (27/28 forecast), 6.30% (28/29 forecast). Absolute financing costs £17.093m → £22.702m over five years, a £5.609m rise.
facts.note: 72 bps of ratio headroom consumed between 25/26 forecast and 27/28 forecast peak. CRMP funding held flat at −£2.632m from 25/26 onwards. PFI/Coed Pella runs down from £3.745m to £2.813m.

LIMITS only. The paper does not print the actual bucket percentages of Conwy's own book. Q3 compliance with all prudential indicators asserted at doc 226476 §3.7 but the underlying percentages sit in the Q3 appendix, which is not held on disk.

facts.value: Bank Rate cut to 3.75% in December (verbatim, p.3). Arlingclose expects Bank Rate to be cut to 3.25% by middle of 2026, with near-term upside risks. Central-case 10-year gilt: 4.52% current → 4.30% by mid-2026. 20-year: 5.16% → 4.90%. 50-year: 4.74% → 4.60%.
facts.note: Testable forecast. Bank Rate at 3.75% today (2026-08-14 market snapshot) — the expected cut to 3.25% has not materialised. PWLB 10-year certainty today is 5.83% (notice 314/26 PM); with the standard 100bps / certainty 80bps margin over gilts, that implies a 10-year gilt yield around 5.0-5.1% — c.70-80bps higher than Arlingclose's mid-2026 forecast of 4.30%.

facts.value: External borrowing decreased £19.5m (from £231.5m to £212.0m) during April to December 2025. Investments decreased £13.2m (from £40.6m to £27.4m) over the same period. Full compliance with prudential indicators asserted.
facts.note: Detail lives in Appendix A of doc 226476 (not held). The £212.0m at 31 December ties exactly to Table 1's £212,022,508 at 8 January 2026 in the strategy paper.

facts.value: Recommended 2026/27 capital programme £40.860m (doc 226479 §3.2), including supported/unsupported borrowing £12.244m, £3.6m already in 2025/26 programme, capital receipts £910k, capital reserves £1.032m, earmarked reserve £300k and grants £22.774m. Full programme running total at 20 January 2026 is £117.070m (£66.693m in 2025/26, £50.377m in later years).
facts.note: Ties to Table 5's £75.062m total 2026/27 capital expenditure and £66.693m for 25/26 revised in Appendix B.

facts.value: Our bc-loans file holds 50 PWLB loans in total for CONWY COUNTY BOROUGH COUNCIL (£172,674,509 principal at draw, weighted 5.00%). 49 are live at 2026-08-15 with balance £161,062,700. The paper reports PWLB £167,522,508 at 8 January 2026 (Table 1, p.2). Gap c.£6.5m (about 3.9%) between our current live and their 8 January position.
facts.note: DOES NOT TIE. The paper prints no weighted rate to check against and no loan-by-loan schedule. The `--as-at 2026-01-08` mode of price_book.py returns only 18 loans / £85.9m — impossible against the paper's own £167.5m — so the Start-field limitation flagged in EMAIL_TEMPLATE.md §7 applies here and the as-at result is discarded. Some paydown between 8 January and 15 August 2026 on 14 EIP loans fits part of the gap; a small residual likely sits with a data-side ledger issue rather than a genuine coverage gap. Disclosed in the email, not raised as an ask.

facts.value: Lead officer: Gareth Evans, Head of Finance. Contact officer on the strategy: Huw Ifor Jones, Principal Accountant. Contact officer on the Q3 report: Huw Jones, Principal Accountant. Portfolio holder: Cllr Chris Cater. No email address is printed on any of the three papers held.
facts.note: No s151 title is printed. Conwy is a Welsh unitary; under the LGA 2003 as applied in Wales the s151 role exists but the paper does not identify who holds it. Do not guess from mg.contacts — the failure mode in EMAIL_TEMPLATE.md §8. The email cannot be sent until an address is added.

reconciliation.balance_sheet_identity: At 31.3.25 actual: Loans CFR £234.188m less external borrowing £237.086m = −£2.898m (over-borrowed by £2.9m) — Table 7 prints +£2.898m over-borrowed. Exact. At 31.3.26 estimate: Loans CFR £253.167m less external £229.986m = +£23.181m (internal) — Table 7 prints −£23.181m under-borrowed. Exact.
reconciliation.loan_book_tie: DOES NOT TIE. bc-loans holds 50 PWLB loans (49 live, balance £161,062,700 at 2026-08-15) against the paper's £167,522,508 at 8 January 2026. Gap c.£6.5m (3.9%). Disclosed in the email as an honest coverage-gap note; not raised as an ask. The paper prints no weighted rate to check against.
reconciliation.table_sums: Table 1 fixed-rate borrowing 167.523 + 34.500 + 10.000 = 212.023 exact. Table 4 net loans requirement + liquidity allowance = liability benchmark each year, exact. Table 5 total expenditure less capital receipts + grants + reserves = net financing need each year, exact. Table 6 movement in loans CFR = financing need less MRP/VRP each year, exact. Table 7 estimated gross debt at 31 March + OLTL = same as sum of prior year debt + change, exact. Table 8 authorised limit = borrowing + OLTL each year, exact.
reconciliation.rates_check: The paper does not print any prevailing PWLB certainty rate at the time of writing (8 January 2026 or thereabouts), only the Arlingclose gilt yield forecast. Not directly comparable to PWLB certainty rates. No rate cross-check possible against Conwy's own paper.

summary.text:
Conwy's 2026/27 Treasury Strategy is a substantive paper with a clear headline: the council flipped from a mildly over-borrowed position at 31 March 2025 (+£2.9m) to £23.2m under-borrowed by 31 March 2026 estimated — a £26.1m swing to internal borrowing inside a single year — and expects to hold that position broadly unchanged (−£22.7m / −£21.7m / −£20.8m) through 2028/29. The Q3 covering report confirms the mechanism: external borrowing dropped £19.5m from April to December 2025 (£231.5m to £212.0m), and investments came down £13.2m alongside. The strategy states the choice explicitly at page 4: with short rates higher than long rates and rates expected to fall, internal or short-medium borrowing is 'more cost effective over the medium-term'.

The forward CFR pressure is real. Loans CFR grows £57.7m across the strategy period (£234.2m at 31.3.25 to £291.9m at 31.3.29), while OLTL runs off £54.3m to £41.9m as PFI and leases mature. Table 9 shows financing costs rising from £17.1m (24/25 actual) to a peak £22.3m in 27/28, and the ratio to net revenue stream climbing from 5.66% (25/26 forecast) to 6.38% (27/28 forecast) before easing 8 bps in 28/29 — 72 bps of headroom consumed at the peak.

The paper is thinner than an outturn or an annual report on loan-level detail: Table 1 (dated 8 January 2026) prints the £212.0m total borrowing split three ways (PWLB £167.5m, other LA £34.5m, market £10.0m) but no weighted rate on any of the three, no maturity buckets by percentage, no loan-by-loan schedule. Table 3 sets refinancing limits (under-12m capped at 40%, 10y+ capped at 75%) but does not print the actual bucket weights. Q3 compliance is asserted at doc 226476 §3.7 but the underlying figures sit in a Q3 appendix (Appendix A of the Q3 item) that is not bundled with the covering PDF and is not on disk.

Balance sheet arithmetic ties exactly at every step. Table 6 (Gross CFR less OLTL equals Loans CFR) foots to the £000 in each of the five years. Table 7's under/over-borrowed row reproduces exactly from the balance-sheet identity applied to Loans CFR and external borrowing. Table 4's liability-benchmark row matches Table 6's Loans CFR row to the £000. The £212.0m external borrowing at 31 December 2025 quoted in the Q3 covering matches Table 1's £212.0m at 8 January 2026 exactly.

Our own PWLB reconciliation does NOT tie: bc-loans holds 49 live loans at £161.1m today against the paper's £167.5m at 8 January 2026 — a c.£6.5m gap (3.9%). The paper prints no weighted rate to check against, and the paper's own maturity profile is not disclosed, so the rate-quote and bucket cross-checks are also unavailable. Adviser: Arlingclose Ltd. The three papers name Gareth Evans (Head of Finance, lead officer), Huw Ifor Jones (Principal Accountant, contact officer on the strategy) and Cllr Chris Cater (Cabinet Member for Finance and Strategic Planning) but publish no email address for any of them, and do not identify the s151 by title. An email has been drafted but cannot be sent until an address is added.

officer.body:
Hi [OFFICER FIRST NAME],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the 2026/27 Treasury Strategy that went to Governance and Audit on 9 February and on to Council on 26 February. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it.

One cross-check first, and one honest disclosure. Your tables reconcile cleanly: Gross CFR less other long-term liabilities equals Loans CFR in Table 6, the same Loans CFR row appears in the liability-benchmark table and again against external borrowing in Table 7, and every year's arithmetic in the (under)/over-borrowed row foots exactly against the balance-sheet identity. Table 1's £212.023m of total borrowing at 8 January 2026 also ties to the £212.0m external borrowing at 31 December 2025 quoted in the Q3 covering. On the PWLB side we hold 49 live loans totalling £161.1m against your Table 1 figure of £167.5m at 8 January — a c.£6.5m gap, or about 3.9%. The paper prints no weighted rate on the book so we can't quote-back a rate, and our own file has some known unreliability on drawdown dates; the gap is more likely to sit on our side than yours, and we mention it so you know the number we're working from rather than to ask you to correct us.

The headline in your paper, once the two years are put side by side, is a £26m move. Table 7 shows Conwy was over-borrowed by £2.9m at 31 March 2025 and expects to be under-borrowed by £23.2m at 31 March 2026 estimate — a £26.1m swing to an internally-borrowed position inside a single year, then held broadly at that level through 2028/29 (−£22.7m, −£21.7m, −£20.8m). The Q3 covering makes the mechanism clean: external borrowing dropped £19.5m between April and December 2025, from £231.5m to £212.0m. Your page 4 explains the choice plainly — with short rates higher than long rates and rates expected to fall, internal or short-medium borrowing is more cost-effective over the medium term. That is a real decision, and rarer in the strategies we read than it should be.

The cost-of-carry maths behind that choice is where the market has an opinion. When your paper was written Arlingclose expected Bank Rate to be cut to 3.25% by the middle of 2026; today, six months on, Bank Rate is still 3.75% — the December cut held but the next one hasn't come. The Arlingclose 10-year gilt central case for later 2026 was 4.30%; PWLB 10-year certainty closed yesterday afternoon at 5.83% on notice 314/26, implying the underlying gilt is around 5.0% — roughly 70 basis points higher than the forecast. Your existing external book is insulated because it's already drawn and 100% fixed. What's exposed is the £38.8m of Loans CFR growth planned across the strategy period (£253m at 31 March 2026 rising to £292m by 31 March 2029, from Table 6), because that block has to be funded either from cash (extending the £23m internal position) or from new external borrowing at today's curve rather than the one Arlingclose was forecasting. Your Table 9 already prices some of this in — financing costs to net revenue stream go 5.66% to 6.38% at the 27/28 peak — but the shape of the funding decision within it is a live one.

Where we might be useful is the tool the CIPFA Prudential and Treasury Code updates put at the centre: the liability benchmark. Your Table 4 climbs from £206m at 31 March 2025 to £264m at 31 March 2029, and the Arlingclose chart on page 7 shows the existing fixed-rate book running off from around £200m today to £80m by 2032. The gap between those two lines is the future new-borrowing requirement, and it's the shape most sensitive to the timing question the strategy raises. We publish live curves underneath the benchmark so the point at which the two lines meet — and the notional cost of closing them — move with the market rather than being recalculated once a year. Yours is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis.

For the market itself: PWLB certainty on 14 August was 4.95% at one year, 5.34% at five, 5.83% at ten, 6.38% at twenty, 6.46% at twenty-five and 6.27% at fifty. July's total sector lending was £368m across just 33 loans from 19 borrowers at an average 5.02% — thin, and worth knowing before you need to be in it. That breakdown is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity.

One smaller observation, for context rather than action. Your PWLB book prices about £0.75m below par on the DMO's premature repayment curve today — a net discount of 0.5% of principal, with 12 of the 49 live loans below par and the largest single discount on the 2067 maturity at 2.30%. Nothing follows from that: we don't sell treasury products, we model no MRP or accounting treatment, only the DMO can quote, and whether anything would be worth doing turns on replacement cost we do not model. It's just where the book sits on today's curve, priced daily.

On training, four fit Conwy. Liability Benchmark: using it in practice goes to your Table 4 and the £58m rise in the benchmark over four years. Internal borrowing — cost-of-carry mechanics goes to the choice you've already made and how the maths tightens if rates don't fall as forecast. Cash-flow forecasting & daily cash sits under the £23m under-borrowed position — how far internal can be pushed depends on the trough of cash, not the average. And PWLB break costs — mechanics & live calculator for the discount position noted above. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix B, Governance and Audit Committee, 9 February 2026 (mg34 doc 226481); Q3 2025/26 covering report (doc 226476); Capital and Treasury Strategy 2026/27 covering report (doc 226479).
